FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Jndian Standards, the Plastics Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Division Council. after the draft finalized by Coal and Related Products.

Plastics strappings are widely used in closing, reinforcing, bundling articles for shipment, unitizing, palletizing and bracing for car laading and truck loading. They are generally manufactured by extrusion of polymeric materials through a slit die and then oriented by stretching, stabilizing and knurling, if need be. Commonly used plastics strapping include, `bonded rayon cord type' which consist of longitudinal rayon cords bonded with a plastic binder such that a non-woven material. is obtained; `bonded or woven polyester cord type' which consists of longitudinal polyester cords bonded with a plastic binder to form a non-woven material or longitudinal polyester cords woven with a weft thread and treated with a binder to form a woven material; `polyolefin type' which is. basically extruded, oriented polyolefins; `Nylon type' which is extruded, oriented nylons and `polyester type' which is extruded oriented polyesters. Of these four types of thermoplastic box. strappings `bonded rayon cord type' and `polyester type' are not manufactured in this country and are also not in use in India. Among the `polyolefin type' mainly polypropylene strappings are widely used; the consumption of polyethylene ( HDPE ) strapp:ngs are very small. Accordingly,. only two types of thermoplastic strappings namely `polyolefin type' and `nylon type' have been covered in this Indian Standard. Only polypropylene strappings among the`polyolefin type' have been covered in this standard. However, HDPE strappings will be includedat a later date as and when sufficient data are made available. It does not This Indian Standard may involve hazardous materials, operations and equipments. purport to address all of the safety problems associated with its use. It is the responsibility of` the user of this standard to establish appropriate safety and health practices and determine the applicability of regulatory limitations prior to use. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with,. the final value. observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised).' The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Strappings shall be clean, straight, free of twists, edge curvature, cracks and other defects that may affect serviceability. Strappings shall be plain or knurled as agreed upon by purchaser and supplier. 7 REQUIREMENTS 7.1 The nominal width, nominal thickness and minimum weight per 1000 metres and the breaking load and elongation at break, when tested as prescribed in Annex A, of Types I and II strappings shall not be less than the corresponding values specified in Tables 1 and 2 respectively. 7.2 The strappings while strapping. 8 PACKJNG -8.1 Packing Strappings, however, may be packed as agreed~to between the purchaser and the supplier. 8.1.1 Strapping shall be wound on a~core of suitable material to support load and prevent collapse during dispensing. Core diameter and core width shall be of proper size. Each coil of strapping shall be secured against unwinding and shall be packed in a close-fitting weatherresistant box. 8.2 Marking shall be non-splitting type

ANNEX A ( Clause 7.1 )
DETERMINATION
A-l A-l.1 AmP'PARATUS Tensile Testing Machine

OF BREAKING

LOAD AND ELONGATIO-N

AT BREAK

Total length of the specimen shall be at least 150 mm longer than the gauge length. A-3 PROCEDURE

The tensile testing machine used shall maintain a rate of traverse of one grip as constant as possible and shall be capable of maintaining the speed of 50 rtr. 2 mm/minute. The load scale The shall be accurate to within one percent. load shall be such that the breaking load of the test pieces falls between 15 percent and 8'5 percent of the full scale reading. The sample clamping grips shall be of hydraulic/pneumatic type to provide firm grip of the sample while testing. A-2 PREPARATION OF TEST SPECIMEN

Condition the test specimen for not less than 24 hours at 27�C f 2% and 65 f 5 percent relative humidity. Clamp the ends of the specimens on the machine at the grips separated at the rate of 50 & 2 mm/minute and note the load and elongation at break. A-4 CALCULATION AND REPORT

The -gauge length of the specimen shall be 125 mm. Cut five test pieces from the sample.

The mean value of breaking loads is reported as minimum breaking load. Elongation at break shall be expressed as percentage of the original length between the grips and the mean value shall be expressed as minimum elongation at break.
